The box below is what the emulator was doing when it stopped. If a game keeps failing, these lines say why.

Pick a game file on your TV. AeonPS2 copies it into its own folder, so it stays put even if the original moves.
Pick your PlayStation 2 BIOS file (usually a .bin file, 4 MB). It gets copied into AeonPS2\'s BIOS folder.
No BIOS yet — import your own PS2 BIOS to play
Remove all BIOS files? Games won\'t start without one.
Could not copy the BIOS file
That file is not 4 MB — a real PlayStation 2 BIOS is exactly 4,194,304 bytes.
This file is the right size for a BIOS (4 MB) but doesn\'t look like a Sony BIOS — games may crash with it.
This file is the right size for a BIOS but doesn\'t look like a PlayStation 2 BIOS at all — games will probably crash with it.
BIOS works — the PlayStation 2 shell started.
BIOS didn\'t start — games won\'t either.
The emulator rejected this BIOS file (it isn\'t a working PS2 BIOS). Try a different dump of your own console.
AeonPS2 needs your own PlayStation 2 BIOS to start anything. Import it on the BIOS screen first.
AeonPS2 closed while playing %1$s last time.
That file is too small to be a PS2 game.
The disc is missing its data file: %1$s
Could not start the emulator core.
The emulator engine file is missing — reinstall AeonPS2.
Could not save the BIOS file.
That file is a PlayStation 2 BIOS, not a game.
Quick-press START in a game: the game\'s own button — that\'s how Kingdom Hearts pauses and Final Fantasy X opens menus. Hold START (about half a second), or press Back: this menu instead.
A save state is a big file (%1$s). Save it anyway?

In a game, a quick press of START goes to the game itself — it\'s the game\'s own button, and Kingdom Hearts pauses with it. To open the AeonPS2 menu instead, hold START for about half a second, or press Back. Both analog sticks work in games that use them.
Core defaults — the tested path. This is how the engine is built to run, and it\'s the mode every fix was proven in.
💾 Virtual hard drive — coming in a later version, not in v1.0
Slim is still being proven — Fat is the tested path. Pick Slim only if you want to help test it.
PS2 games are heavy. Light games run best on a TV stick.
Engine: PCEE2 — the PCSX2 engine, the main engine. This TV can run it.
Engine: Play! — the 32-bit fallback engine. This TV can\'t run the main PCSX2 engine, so Play! does the job instead. Expect lower compatibility and speed than the main engine.

No [Test BIOS] here: this TV runs the Play! fallback engine, which can only boot with a game loaded — a no-game boot would crash it. Just launch your game instead; the library and BIOS import work the same.
